title: PUT accepts explicit nulls for optional update fields and can persist invalid values or raise 500
reasoning: Partial-update schemas often use optional fields to mean 'field may be omitted', but update_feed treats explicitly provided null values as real writes. For required feed properties such as title, mode, max_articles, and is_active, a request body like {"title": null} reaches setattr and then commit. Depending on database nullability this either stores an invalid feed shape or raises an integrity error that becomes a 500 instead of a validation error. Confidence is medium because the included tests do not define the null-input contract, but the route currently has no guard against null writes.
reproduction: PUT /api/feeds/{id} with {"title": null} or {"max_articles": null} after creating a feed. The handler includes the key because exclude_unset=True does not exclude explicit nulls, then writes None before committing.
recommendation: Reject explicit nulls for fields that are not nullable in the feed domain, either by using non-null field types with an unset sentinel/update model validator or by filtering/validating None values before setattr and returning 422.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests do not exercise PUT /{feed_id} at all, and they only assert happy-path create/sync behavior with non-null values.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a PUT test that sends {"title": null} and asserts a 422 response and that the existing feed title remains unchanged.
minimumFixScope: FeedUpdate validation or app/api/feeds.py update_feed null handling, plus one regression test
